name: Józef Piłsudski
role: Polish Chief of State (1918-1922), Marshal and de facto ruler of Poland after the 1926 coup (died 1935)
summary: Piłsudski, a former socialist who made Polish independence his first aim, led Poland's 1918-22 state, doubted parliamentary government and took power by coup in 1926, favoured a federal alliance of eastern European states only by consent, and opposed expulsions of Jews and chauvinism.

sources.title: Józef Piłsudski, Pisma, mowy, rozkazy: wydanie zbiorowe prac dotychczas drukiem ogłoszonych, vol. 1 (Warsaw 1930-1933), RCIN scan on Internet Archive (Polish)
sources.author: Józef Piłsudski
sources.usedFor: Early writings and correspondence for Przedświt, 1890s-1900s: socialism and Polish independence, anti-chauvinism, the expulsion of Jews from Russia.

sources.title: Józef Piłsudski, Pisma, mowy, rozkazy: wydanie zbiorowe prac dotychczas drukiem ogłoszonych, vol. 5 (Warsaw 1930-1933), RCIN scan on Internet Archive (Polish)
sources.author: Józef Piłsudski
sources.usedFor: Speeches and orders as Chief of State, 1918-1920, including the Vilnius territory question.

sources.title: Józef Piłsudski, Pisma, mowy, rozkazy: wydanie zbiorowe prac dotychczas drukiem ogłoszonych, vol. 6 (Warsaw 1930-1933), RCIN scan on Internet Archive (Polish)
sources.author: Józef Piłsudski
sources.usedFor: Speeches and interviews 1921-1925, including the Słowo Wileńskie interview of 14 August 1923 on parliamentarism.

sources.title: Józef Piłsudski, Pisma, mowy, rozkazy, vol. 2 (Warsaw 1930-1933), RCIN scan on Internet Archive (Polish): 'Jak stałem się socjalistą' (How I became a socialist)
sources.author: Józef Piłsudski
sources.usedFor: His account of how he came to socialism and why a Polish socialist must strive for national independence.

sources.title: Rozporządzenie Prezydenta Rzeczypospolitej z dnia 17 czerwca 1934 r. w sprawie osób zagrażających bezpieczeństwu, spokojowi i porządkowi publicznemu, Dziennik Ustaw 1934 nr 50 poz. 473 (eli.gov.pl PDF), countersigned by the Minister of Military Affairs J. Piłsudski
sources.author: President Ignacy Mościcki and ministers including Józef Piłsudski
sources.usedFor: The decree under which persons whose conduct suggests a threat to security could be seized and placed in isolation camps (Bereza Kartuska) without trial for three months, renewable.

sources.title: Józef Piłsudski, Wikipedia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Orientation to his career (Chief of State 1918-22, the 1926 coup, Sanacja), used to locate the primary texts.

his collected writings (cited) are speeches and orders up to 1923 and do not cover them

notes: First audit. Read by theme in volumes 1, 5 and 6 of the 1930-33 collected 'Pisma, mowy, rozkazy' (Polish OCR; translations are mine, so confidence stays at medium at most): early socialist writings, speeches as Chief of State on Vilnius and federation, and the 1923 interview on parliamentarism. Volume 2 ('How I became a socialist', Bibuła, the revolutionary struggle) is read for his socialism; volumes 3 (military organisation, Balkan war articles, the Vienna Social Democrats speech), 4 (Legion orders, Magdeburg letters, the Council of State) and 7 (the 1920 campaign narrative) were searched for socialism, Jews, the Church, the Sejm, the constitution and conscription and are military or organisational, with no further statement on the test's themes than those cited. In 1920 he said the principle of federation could not be applied by arms to the eastern lands and told of wanting facts on the ground first; that is a claim about method, not a statement on the test's statements, and stays null. His act record is cited from the 17 June 1934 decree he countersigned (Dziennik Ustaw poz. 473). The April 1935 Constitution (Dz.U. 1935 poz. 227) was read but is not attributed to him: it was signed by the President Mościcki and does not name him. The May 1926 coup and the 1930 Brest arrests were not found in an open primary or scholarly source and are not answered.
